subject: chemistry
title: Energetics & Thermochemistry Adventure 2: Hess's law and bond enthalpies
welcome_lead: Today you'll use Hess's law to find unmeasurable ΔH values.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — Hess's law, energy cycles, bond enthalpy, mean bond enthalpy.
final_note: You learned Hess's law states ΔH depends only on initial and final states, and bond enthalpies estimate ΔH via bonds broken minus bonds made.

concepts.def: Energy to break 1 mol of bonds (g)

walkthroughs.body_html:
'The enthalpy change is independent of route.'

If A → B = +50 kJ via one path, it's +50 kJ via any other.

This works because H is a state function.

Construct cycles linking unknown ΔH to known ΔH (combustion, formation).

Find ΔH for C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g).

Known: ΔH_c(C) = -394 (C→CO₂); ΔH_c(CO) = -283 (CO→CO₂).

Cycle: C → CO → CO₂, also C → CO₂.
ΔH(C→CO) + ΔH(CO→CO₂) = ΔH(C→CO₂)
ΔH(C→CO) = -394 − (-283) = -111 kJ/mol.

Estimate ΔH:

ΔH ≈ Σ bonds broken − Σ bonds made

For CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(g):
Broken: 4 C-H (412) + 2 O=O (496) = 1648 + 992 = 2640.
Made: 2 C=O (805) + 4 O-H (463) = 1610 + 1852 = 3462.
ΔH = 2640 − 3462 = -822 kJ/mol.

Note: mean values, gaseous, and only approximate.
